description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Winawer Countergambit. Meet 3...e5 with calm development.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Nc3 e5 4.dxe5 d4 5.Nf3! — take, then develop; don't fear the wedge.
drills.description: White to play. Black may try the countergambit 3...e5 — develop 3.Nc3 and know the reply.
drills.explanation: The calm antidote: after 3...e5 4.dxe5 d4, White plays 5.Nf3! — developing and ignoring the pawn. Black's d4 wedge looks scary but White will undermine it with e3; the extra pawn (e5) is real, and Black's 'initiative' needs a target that White won't provide. Take the pawn, develop, undermine.
drills.name: The Calm Nf3

drills.briefExplanation: 5.e3! dxe3 6.Bxe3 Nf6 7.Nf3 — undermine, develop with tempo, complete the setup.
drills.description: White to play. Black pushed 4...d4 — undermine with 5.e3!.
drills.explanation: The direct refutation of the wedge: 5.e3! challenges d4 immediately. After 5...dxe3 6.Bxe3 White develops with tempo, the center opens for the bishops, and Black's gambit pawn is gone — White keeps the e5 pawn and the better structure. Undermine advanced wedges at their base.
drills.name: The e3 Undermining

name: Winawer Countergambit — White Tactics
